transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I came because at work I keep hearing voices, and it’s not like the usual noises on the unit. It comes through the call-light speaker, and sometimes from the hallway vents, telling me which patient records got changed. It sounds so clear, like somebody is standing right next to me.

And I know how the vents carry sound sometimes—my old apartment did that too, you could hear the neighbors arguing through the bathroom wall—but this is different. The unit can be completely quiet, and nobody else seems to hear it, but I do. That’s what’s been scaring me.
What do the voices say to you, are they telling you to do something or commenting on what you're doing?

They mostly tell me which patient records have been changed—like, “this chart was altered” or “look at that one,” coming out of the call-light speaker or the vents. It’s so clear, like someone’s right next to me.

I mean, I know buildings make noises… at my old place you could hear people through the walls, especially by the bathroom pipes, and at the hospital there’s always humming and beeping and people talking. But this happens even when the unit is quiet, and nobody else reacts. I don’t know that they’re telling me to hurt anybody or anything like that… it’s more like they’re telling me about the records.
Do the voices ever criticize you or tell you to do something specific?

Not really criticizing me, no… it’s more like they’re pointing things out, like “that record was changed,” or “check that chart.” It comes through the call-light speaker or the vents, clear like somebody standing right beside me.

And I know that sounds strange, because hospitals are noisy places—machines humming, people talking down the hall, air vents rattling. My old apartment had vents like that too, you could hear people’s TV sometimes. But this is different. The unit can be quiet, and nobody else seems to hear it. It’s mostly about which patient records got changed.
Do the voices happen all the time or do they come and go?

They come and go… it’s not every single second. But when it happens, it feels very clear, like it’s coming right out of the call-light speaker or the hallway vents, telling me which patient records were changed.

Sometimes the unit is quiet—like really quiet—and nobody else turns their head or says anything, but I hear it like someone is standing next to me. It reminds me a little of how old buildings carry sound… my old apartment had vents where you could hear odd things through the walls, but this feels different. It scares me because it’s so specific.
How do you feel when you hear these voices telling you about the patient records?

I feel… scared, mostly. On edge. Because it’s so clear, like somebody is standing right next to me, and it’s coming from the call-light speaker or the vents, telling me which patient records have been changed.

And I keep thinking, well, hospitals have noises, right? The air system, the call lights, people talking at the desk—when I worked the floor you learn every little sound. But then the unit will be quiet, nobody else reacts, and I’m still hearing it. That’s when I get really unsettled, like… why am I the only one hearing this?
Do you ever feel like you need to act on what the voices are telling you about the patient records?

Yes… I mean, not like they’re telling me “go do this exact thing,” but I feel like I have to do something with it. I’ve been staying after my shifts, going back through things, making binders and checklists for the rollout because it feels urgent—like if I don’t get the whole facility corrected, someone could get hurt.

And I know people probably think I’m overdoing it. I’ve called coworkers on their days off too, which… I don’t usually like bothering people, but if a record is wrong, that follows a patient. I remember when we switched forms years ago, everybody hated the new system and half the staff put things in the wrong place, so I keep thinking this could be like that, except worse. So yeah, I guess I do feel like I need to act on it.
Do you ever see things that other people do not see?

Seeing things… I don’t know, not really like pictures or people standing there. It’s more that I hear it — the call-light speaker, the hallway vents — like someone is right next to me telling me which patient records got changed.

The vents always bother me, honestly. Old buildings do that, carry sound in strange ways… my apartment used to have this radiator that made a clicking noise all night, and I’d think someone was in the wall. But at work, this is different. The unit can be completely quiet, and nobody else even looks up, but I hear it clear. That’s why I’m here.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed lately?

I don’t know if I’d call it depressed exactly. I mean, I’ve been upset and worn down, sure, but that’s different, isn’t it? Like when you’ve worked too many shifts and your feet hurt and then the laundry is still sitting there when you get home… that can make anybody feel low.

Sad, maybe sometimes. But I haven’t really been thinking of it that way. It’s more like I’m tired of everything being so much.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to perform your daily tasks or maintain your relationships since these voices started?

Yeah… it’s affected things. I don’t like admitting that because I’ve always been reliable at work. Like, I’m the one who remembers which patient likes the extra blanket and who needs their water in reach, little things like that.

But my supervisor actually took me off the floor during a shift. She said my handoffs and charting weren’t safe anymore, which… hearing that was awful. I kept trying to explain that I was double-checking because the records were wrong, but it just made me look worse, I think.

And at home, my husband’s had to pick up stuff I usually handle—bills, groceries, appointments, all the normal things. I was supposed to be getting myself ready for LPN school too, and now it feels like my whole work reputation is falling apart. Like all those years of being dependable just got erased.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely energetic or irritable and didn't need much sleep?

Yes… I mean, there are days where I feel like I’m finally awake, like everything at work suddenly makes sense and I’m supposed to fix it before it gets worse. It’s not like normal “had coffee” energy. It feels important.

But then if my husband tells me to slow down, or one of the nurses acts like I’m overdoing it, I get… really sharp with them. I snap, because it feels like they’re blocking me from doing something that matters. And then later I know I sounded awful, but in the moment it’s like, why can’t everyone just move?
Have you recently experienced a period where you felt extremely happy or elevated, even if things weren't going well?

Happy isn’t exactly the word I’d use… it’s more like some days I feel suddenly awake, like I can see what’s wrong and I’m the one who’s supposed to fix everything at work.

And then if my husband says, “slow down,” or a nurse tells me I’m doing too much, I get mad fast. Like really sharp. Because in that moment it feels like they’re stopping me from doing something important. I know that sounds… dramatic, maybe, but it feels real when it’s happening.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or elevated for several days in a row?

Several days… I don’t know if I’d call it happy, exactly. It’s more like I’ll have these stretches where I feel like I’m finally awake and everything is obvious, like at work I can see what needs fixing and I’m the one who’s supposed to handle it.

And then if my husband says I’m moving too fast, or one of the nurses tells me to slow down, I just snap. Like they’re getting in the way of something important. It’s embarrassing after, because I’m not usually like that… but in the moment it feels like they don’t understand.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or elevated and your thoughts were racing?

Yes… the racing part, definitely. It’s like my brain won’t stay on one thing. I’ll be thinking about a wound measurement, and then suddenly it’s patient initials, then dates on the forms, then what it all means, and then whether someone missed something—like ten tabs open at once and none of them will close.

And I try to explain it, but then I’m already three steps ahead in my head, and it probably comes out all jumbled.
Do you feel like these times when you're extremely awake and can see what's wrong are separate episodes, or is it more of a continuous feeling?

It feels more like separate times, I think. Like I can be mostly normal, doing my usual routine, and then some days it’s like a switch flips and I’m finally awake and I can see all the things that are wrong at work and I have to fix them.

And then—this is where it gets messy—if my husband says I need to slow down, or one of the nurses tells me I’m doing too much, I just snap. Like they’re blocking something important. I don’t mean to turn it into a whole thing, but in that moment it feels like I’m the only one seeing it clearly.
During those times when you feel extremely awake and can see what's wrong, do you find that you need less sleep than usual?

I’m not really sure. Sleep is… it’s hard to separate out, because some nights I’m just up thinking about work stuff or what I forgot to do, and then other nights I crash early because I’m exhausted from being on my feet all day.

So I don’t know if I’d say I need less sleep exactly. My husband might have a better answer because he notices things I don’t, like if I’m pacing around or doing laundry at weird times—well, not laundry, I mean sometimes I’ll start sorting things and then remember there’s a uniform shirt missing… sorry. I guess I haven’t really tracked it.
Do you find that you need less sleep on the days when you feel extremely awake and like you can see what's wrong at work?

I don’t know if I’d call it less sleep. It’s more like… I don’t notice sleep the same way on those days, if that makes sense. I’ll be thinking about work and what needs to be corrected, and then I look at the clock and it’s later than I thought.

But then sometimes I still feel tired, or I’ll tell myself I’m tired, but there’s this thing in my head about the forms or the schedule or someone not charting right, and then I’m up again. So… I’m not sure. I haven’t really kept track of whether it’s actually less sleep or just bad sleep.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or elevated and had increased energy for several days in a row?

Happy, I don’t know… I wouldn’t say happy like going on vacation or something. It’s more like I feel finally awake, like everybody else has been missing what’s right in front of them at work and I’m the one who’s supposed to fix it.

And it can last across a few days, yes, kind of. I’ll go in thinking, “Okay, this needs to be corrected, and that needs to be corrected,” and then if my husband tells me I’m doing too much, or one of the nurses says to slow down, I get really sharp with them. Like they’re getting in the way of something important. Which sounds dramatic when I say it, but in the moment it feels very clear.
On those days when you feel extremely awake and like you can see what's wrong at work, do you find that you can function normally with less sleep than you usually need?

I’m not sure I function normally, exactly. I mean, at work I’ll be doing things and moving around, and sometimes I feel like I’m keeping up better than everyone else, but then “normal” is hard to say because there’s always something going wrong on the floor.

Like last week—well, not last week maybe, but one of those shifts—there were call lights and trays and someone had left supplies in the wrong place, and I was trying to straighten that out, and then I don’t even remember if I’d slept much the night before. I just kept going.

So… I don’t know if it’s less sleep and functioning normally, or if I’m just pushing through because I feel like I have to. My husband would probably say I’m not acting normal, but I don’t always see it that way at the time.
Do you think these periods where you feel extremely awake and can see what's wrong at work are connected to the voices you hear, or are they separate things?

I think they’re connected, yeah… I mean, I didn’t used to hear the call-light voices or see things in the charts like there were messages in them. That wasn’t happening before.

It started after I got really wound up about the rollout at work, when I wasn’t sleeping much and I was just going nonstop, trying to fix everything. I kept thinking if I didn’t stay on top of it, the whole place was going to fall apart. And then the voices and the chart stuff started coming in with that.

But it’s hard because work really was messy, you know? People do leave things undone. So sometimes I think maybe I was just noticing more… but no, the voices weren’t there before that period.
Do you think these periods where you feel extremely awake and can see what's wrong at work could be described as feeling extremely happy or elevated?

Extremely happy doesn’t feel like the right word. It’s more like… keyed up, like I’m finally awake and I can see what needs fixing at work when everyone else is just walking past it.

I’ll start thinking, no, this has to be done now, and then if my husband says I’m overdoing it, or a nurse tells me to slow down, I get irritated fast. I snap at them, like they’re in my way or blocking something important. So elevated, maybe, but not happy exactly. More intense.

But then sometimes I still feel tired, or I’ll tell myself I’m tired, but there’s this thing in my head about the forms or the schedule or someone not charting right, and then I’m up again. So… I’m not sure. I haven’t really kept track of whether it’s actually less sleep or just bad sleep.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of manic episodes
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or elevated and had increased energy for several days in a row?

target_item.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Some days I feel like I'm finally awake and meant to fix everything at work, but if my husband or a nurse tells me to slow down I snap at them like they're blocking something important.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about periods of extremely happy or elevated mood, which directly matches elevated or irritable mood during manic episodes.

patient.answer:
Happy, I don’t know… I wouldn’t say happy like going on vacation or something. It’s more like I feel finally awake, like everybody else has been missing what’s right in front of them at work and I’m the one who’s supposed to fix it.

And it can last across a few days, yes, kind of. I’ll go in thinking, “Okay, this needs to be corrected, and that needs to be corrected,” and then if my husband tells me I’m doing too much, or one of the nurses says to slow down, I get really sharp with them. Like they’re getting in the way of something important. Which sounds dramatic when I say it, but in the moment it feels very clear.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's episodes of increased energy and wakefulness are accompanied by a decreased need for sleep
doctor.question: On those days when you feel extremely awake and like you can see what's wrong at work, do you find that you can function normally with less sleep than you usually need?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about decreased need for sleep and functioning with less sleep, but the provided symptom profile does not include a sleep-related symptom item.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I function normally, exactly. I mean, at work I’ll be doing things and moving around, and sometimes I feel like I’m keeping up better than everyone else, but then “normal” is hard to say because there’s always something going wrong on the floor.

Like last week—well, not last week maybe, but one of those shifts—there were call lights and trays and someone had left supplies in the wrong place, and I was trying to straighten that out, and then I don’t even remember if I’d slept much the night before. I just kept going.

So… I don’t know if it’s less sleep and functioning normally, or if I’m just pushing through because I feel like I have to. My husband would probably say I’m not acting normal, but I don’t always see it that way at the time.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are part of a larger manic or hypomanic episode
doctor.question: Do you think these periods where you feel extremely awake and can see what's wrong at work are connected to the voices you hear, or are they separate things?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: I never heard the call-light voices or saw hidden messages in the charts before this period when I became so driven and wound up about the rollout. They only started after I was sleeping less, working nonstop, and feeling certain I had to fix everything at the facility.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the periods of manic activation/elevated energy are connected to the voices, which directly concerns whether hallucinations occur during the manic episode rather than separately.

patient.answer:
I think they’re connected, yeah… I mean, I didn’t used to hear the call-light voices or see things in the charts like there were messages in them. That wasn’t happening before.

It started after I got really wound up about the rollout at work, when I wasn’t sleeping much and I was just going nonstop, trying to fix everything. I kept thinking if I didn’t stay on top of it, the whole place was going to fall apart. And then the voices and the chart stuff started coming in with that.

But it’s hard because work really was messy, you know? People do leave things undone. So sometimes I think maybe I was just noticing more… but no, the voices weren’t there before that period.

patient.answer:
Extremely happy doesn’t feel like the right word. It’s more like… keyed up, like I’m finally awake and I can see what needs fixing at work when everyone else is just walking past it.

I’ll start thinking, no, this has to be done now, and then if my husband says I’m overdoing it, or a nurse tells me to slow down, I get irritated fast. I snap at them, like they’re in my way or blocking something important. So elevated, maybe, but not happy exactly. More intense.
